chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd al-Ijaly, and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both), who said:

Regarding the charity (Zakat) of camels: in every five, one sheep, until it reaches twenty-five. So when it reaches that, then regarding it is a Bint Makhad (a one-year-old female camel). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches thirty-five. So when it reaches thirty-five, then regarding it is a Bint Labun (a two-year-old female camel). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches forty-five. So when it reaches forty-five, then regarding it is a Hiqqah Taruqat al-Fahl (a three-year-old female camel left with the stallion). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches sixty. So when it reaches sixty, then regarding it is a Jadh'ah (a four-year-old female camel).

Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches seventy-five. So when it reaches seventy-five, then regarding it are two Bintay Labun (two two-year-old female camels). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches ninety. So when it reaches ninety, then regarding it are two Hiqqatay Taruqata al-Fahl (two three-year-old female camels left with the stallion). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches one hundred and twenty. So when it reaches one hundred and twenty, then regarding it are two Hiqqatay Taruqata al-Fahl (two three-year-old female camels left with the stallion).

So when one increases upon one hundred and twenty, then regarding every fifty is a Hiqqah (three-year-old female camel), and regarding every forty is a Bint Labun (two-year-old female camel). Then the camels return to their ages (the cycle repeats). And there is nothing upon the 'Nayyif' (the extra ten in a round number like 130, 140, etc.), and there is nothing upon the fractions (remainders less than the threshold), and there is nothing upon the working camels. Rather, that is upon the Saimah al-Ra'iyah (the grazing herd).
He said: I said, 'Is there anything regarding the Bukt al-Saimah (the mixed-breed grazing camels)?' He said: 'Similar to what is regarding the Arabian camels.'

key_terms.النَّيْف: The extra ten in a round number (e.g., the '3' in 130)
key_terms.طَرُوقَةُ الْفَحْلِ: Left with the stallion (not yet bred)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific Zakat rates for different numbers of camels in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent Four Scholars (al-Arba'ah) and narrated by the trusted companions of the Imams, establishes the precise 'nisab' and 'khums' structure for camel Zakat, reflecting the detailed jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt. It distinguishes between the grazing herd (Saimah) eligible for tax and working animals, while the concluding dialogue clarifies that mixed-breed camels (Bukht) are subject to the same rules as purebred Arab camels, ensuring uniformity in charitable obligations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd Al Ijaly, and Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws and Abu Abdullahasws both having said: ‘Regarding charity (Zakāt) of the camels - in every five, one sheep, until it reaches twenty five (camels). So when it reaches that, so regarding these would be one female newborn. Then there would be nothing regarding it until it reaches thirty-five. So when it does reach thirty five, so regarding these would be a two year old female camel giving milk. Then there would be nothing regarding it until it reaches forty-five. So when it does reach forty-five, so regarding these would be a three year old female camel left with a stallion. Then there would be nothing regarding it until it reaches sixty. So when it does reach sixty, so regarding these would be a four year old female camel. Then there would be nothing regarding these until it reaches seventy-five. So when it reaches seventy five, so regarding these would be two two-year old females giving milk. Then there would be nothing regarding these until it reaches ninety. So when it does reach ninety, so regarding these would be two three-year old female camels left with a stallion. Then there would be nothing regarding these until it reaches one hundred and twenty. So when it does reach one hundred and twenty, so regarding these would be two three year old females left with a stallion. So when one increases upon one hundred and twenty, so regarding every fifty would be a three year old female camel, and regarding every forty would be a two year old female camel giving milk. Then the camel would be returned upon its years. And there would be nothing upon the in between numbers and the fractions, and there would be nothing upon the working camels. But rather, that is upon the ones left to pasture’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘What is regarding the running camels, anything?’ Heasws said: ‘Similar to what is regarding the Arabian camels’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, abu Basir, Burayd al-‘ljliy and al-Fudayl who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said that

the amount of Zakat on camel is one sheep for every five camels, until they number twenty-five in which case it is one Ibnatu Makhad. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches thirty-five, in which case Zakat is one Ibnatu Labun. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches forty-five, in which case Zakat is one Hiqqah Taruqah al-Fahl. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches sixty, in which case Zakat is one Jadha‘ah.

Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches seventy-five, in which case Zakat is Ibnata Labun. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches ninety, in which case Zakat is Hiqqatan Taruqat al-Fahl. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat until the number reaches one hundred twenty, in which case Zakat is Hiqqatan Taruqata al-Fahl.

If one more camel increases, thereafter, on every fifty, Zakat is one Hiqqah and on every forty, Zakat is one Ibnatu Labun. All additional camels from this point on are calculated according to the numbers already mentioned. Zakat is not due on what is between two numbers as well as on fractions, or working camels. Only camels that graze in pastures are subject to Zakat.
He (the narrator) has said that he then asked, Is non- Arabic camel which grazes subject to Zakat? 5 He (the Imam) said, It is just like Arabic camels.”
